articles.title: Rupee likely to open flat as dollar strength, US bond yields weigh on sentiment
articles.excerpt:
The Indian rupee is expected to open largely flat against the US dollar on Monday amid mixed global cues.

The Indian rupee is expected to open largely flat on Monday, caught between higher US bond yields, dollar strength and volatile oil prices, while a revival in foreign portfolio inflows cushions the pressure.

The rupee is expected to open in the 94.22 to 94.28 range, according to traders, having settled at 94.24 to the dollar on Friday.

The currency, which had been on a winning run, came under pressure late last week, largely weighed down by a surge in US Treasury yields that lifted the dollar index to its highest level in a year and a half.

articles.excerpt:
SINGAPORE, Nov 16 (Reuters) - The yen was pinned near two-month lows against the dollar and little moved against the euro in early trade on Monday as markets assessed how an unexpected contraction in the Japanese economy in the third quarter affects the policy outlook.

The yen fluctuated between gains and losses without moving too far, trading against the dollar at 159.69 yen and against the euro at 176.04 yen, close to levels where US and Japanese authorities are believed to have intervened earlier this year.

articles.excerpt:
(Bloomberg) -- It took gold just one month to climb more than 30% to a record, but its likely to take another two years before the precious metal takes out a new peak, according to Goldman Sachs.

The bank expects further weakness and heightened volatility in the near term as continued Federal Reserve tightening weighs on non-yielding bullion.

“Once the Fed starts cutting, we expect Western ETF demand to recover, supporting a stronger gold rally to $5,600/ounce by end-2028,” strategists led by Lina Thomas wrote in a note Monday, adding gold prices could rally if macro-policy hedge demand were to return.
